subject: Aligning transition support, notice windows, and termination-for-convenience - BlueLayer pilot
messages:
From: Kelly Huang <kelly@bluelayer.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <legal@bluelayer.io>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: BlueLayer MSA redlines — term, auto-renew, transition support

Marcus — attaching our redlines to the MSA for the pilot (BlueLayer-Redline_MSA_05122026.pdf). Two items that are blocking procurement on our side: 

1) Auto-renew / notice window: We can't commit to auto-renew unless there's a clear opt-out window. Our procurement team is asking for a 45-day written notice before renewal rather than the 60 days in your draft.

2) Termination for convenience + transition support: We need a mutual termination-for-convenience right, and if exercised we'd want 60 days of transitional support (including data export assistance and access to logs) or a pro rata refund for unused months. We flagged data export timing (we require a 30-day export window after termination).

Tom and I would like your legal/ops team's view on: (a) mutual vs. customer-only termination-for-convenience, (b) whether Redwood can commit to a 45-day notice instead of 60, and (c) the exact scope of transitional support (SLA and deliverables).

Can we schedule a 30-minute legal sync this week? We're available Thu 11:00-12:30 PT or Fri 09:00-11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Kelly Huang
Director, Procurement — BlueLayer
kelly@bluelayer.io

Attachment: BlueLayer-Redline_MSA_05122026.pdf (PDF, 1 page redline summary)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kelly Huang <kelly@bluelayer.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueLayer MSA redlines — term, auto-renew, transition support

Kelly — thanks for the clear redlines and quick turn. Appreciate Tom/you flagging the procurement constraints. High-level responses below; copying Legal and Priyom (AM) to keep the commercial side in the loop.

1) Auto-renew / notice window: For enterprise pilots we typically offer a 12-month term with automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms unless either party provides notice. We're willing to make the opt-out window configurable by tier. For BlueLayer's pilot we can accept a 45-day written notice (mutual) instead of 60, provided the Order Form is annotated to show this deviation.

2) Termination for convenience: We can agree a mutual termination-for-convenience right. Standard Redwood position is 60 days' notice for convenience and 90 days' transition support for larger commitments. For pilots, we're prepared to offer 60 days of transition support (data export, KV cache handoff, retained access to logs for 30 days) or a pro-rata credit. We'll have Legal draft exact language; see attached response doc (ms_redline_response_05122026.docx) with suggested edits and a proposed fallback (pro-rata credit if Redwood cannot deliver the transition scope).

Next steps: 
- Legal (Mina): can you review the redline and confirm whether the mutual 45-day renewal opt-out + mutual termination-for-convenience (60d notice / 60d transition) is acceptable from a risk perspective, or if you want to stick to 90d transition?
- Priyom: I'll lock a commercial note that BlueLayer gets 45-day opt-out in the Order Form if Legal signs off.
- Kelly: Thu 11:00 PT works for me; let's tentatively book Thu 2026-05-14 11:00 PT. If that collides with your calendar, Fri AM is also fine.

Marcus
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachment: ms_redline_response_05122026.docx (Word doc with inline suggestions)

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BlueLayer MSA redlines — term, auto-renew, transition support

Thanks Marcus — quick legal read below. I will prepare redline language but want to flag a couple of risk/ops items for the team to consider before finalizing: 

• Mutual 45-day renewal opt-out: acceptable. We should ensure the Order Form is explicit (Order Form overrides MSA standard 60-day default).

• Mutual termination-for-convenience: acceptable in principle, but we should limit financial exposure. Proposed compromise: mutual termination-for-convenience with 60 days' notice and either (i) 60 days' transitional assistance (per scope below) OR (ii) pro-rata refund of pre-paid fees for unused time. For larger commitments (> $250k TCV) we typically keep 90d transition; for a pilot this is reasonable at 60d.

• Transition scope: recommend we list deliverables rather than open-ended SLAs. Suggested bullets to include in redline: 
  - Export of customer data in standard formats (JSON/CSV) within 30 days of effective termination date;
  - One week of scheduled knowledge-transfer sessions (up to 3 x 2-hour sessions) to support handoff;
  - Read-only access to logs and telemetry for 30 days;
  - Option to purchase extended support (30/60/90 day increments) at published rates.

I'll draft the MSA language and attach to an email by EOD. If the team prefers 90d transition, note we'll want that approved by Finance for potential credit exposure.

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Mina — thanks for the fast turnaround and for proposing concrete language. We discussed internally and can accept the mutual termination-for-convenience with 60 days' notice and the transition scope you outlined, but procurement asks for a 45-day renewal opt-out instead of 60 — sounds like you're OK with that if it's in the Order Form, so we're aligned there.

One small ask: can Redwood make the data export window 45 days (instead of 30) to give our SRE time to validate and ingest dumps during the hand-off? If that is acceptable, we can confirm the pilot Order Form and have our legal return a countersigned MSA next week.

Confirming Thu 2026-05-14 11:00 PT for the legal sync — we'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute call.

Appreciate the flexibility — excited to move the pilot live.

Best,
Kelly Huang
Director, Procurement — BlueLayer
kelly@bluelayer.io
